# Week 6

## 2026/10/28

The first half of this week was spent preparing the slides for the presentation.

The slides are designed for a general physics audience and follow the following structure:

1. A brief overview of the project
    - Describing the aims and physical phenomena being observed
2. An introductory theory slide
    - Defining the key terms
        - AGN
        - Accretion disk
        - ISCO
        - Black hole spin
3. A motivations slide
    - Motivating the project with
        - Strong field tests of general relativity
        - Direct measurements of the black hole spin
        - Direct probing of the extreme environments surrounding black holes
4. A theory slide describing the emission mechanisms of AGN reflection
    - Hot corona emitting in X-ray
    - Emission backscattered from the accretion disk
    - Produces a characterstic spectrum as shown with a diagram
    - Mention that we will focus on the iron K`\alpha` line
5. A theory slide describing how emission line broadening occurs
6. A theory slide describing how emission line broadening depends on the spin of the AGN
7. A slide covering the current work
    - Extracting data products
    - Preliminary power law fitting
    - Broad iron line clearly visible
8. A slide on future plans
    - Fitting with RELXILL
    - Fitting alternative model
    - Compiling data and measurements
9. Summary slide

I have also prepared two appendix slides on AGN structure, and iron K$\alpha$ emission.

A bare-bones rehearsal took 06:30 minutes, providing a lot of breathing room to cover the content in greater depth.
